title: BCIR training corpus retrieval chunk (Tier 2)
description: One embedding-ready unit of corpus text. Deterministic: the same source tree always produces the same chunks with the same identifiers. The embedding vector is NEVER produced by the chunker -- a chunk carries `embedding: null` until a named model fills it, because a fabricated vector is indistinguishable from a real one downstream.

chunk_id.description: sha256 over the canonical identity tuple (subject, source_path, heading_trail, text). Content-addressed, so reordering a file does not renumber its chunks and editing one does not disturb its neighbours.

subject.description: The training/<subject>/ folder this chunk came from.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the whole source file, so a chunk can be shown stale without re-reading the corpus.

span.description: 1-indexed inclusive line range in source_path. Lets a retrieved chunk be traced back to the exact lines a human can open.

heading_trail.description: Markdown heading ancestry, outermost first. Prepended to `text` as retrieval context instead of raw token overlap: deterministic, and it does not duplicate neighbouring content.

kind.description: prose = narrative only; code = a single fenced block; mixed = narrative containing fenced blocks; table = a markdown table.

language.description: Fence language for code/mixed chunks; null otherwise.

token_estimate.description: Model-independent estimate used only for budgeting chunk size. Not a tokenizer output and must not be treated as one.

embedding.description: null until a named embedding model fills it. A chunker that invented a vector here would produce records no consumer could distinguish from measured ones.

verified_by.description: Repository-relative gates that check the source file this chunk came from. An empty list is legal and meaningful: it marks unverified prose, which a consumer may weight down or exclude.
